name: Draw a World
description: Draw a line. Watch it become unfinished architecture. Then travel inside your own drawing.

assets.credit: Original perspective construction drawing · Tampa Curated

compatibility: Current Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge with WebGL2 and ES modules. Drawing and JSON export remain available if 3D graphics are unavailable.
Mouse, trackpad, pen, and touch. Keyboard users can choose a path, edit points with arrow keys, and travel with the slider or arrow keys.
Reduced motion applies changes immediately. Rendering sleeps when settled, paused, hidden, or outside the viewport.
No JavaScript: the architectural study plate, instructions, and default source download remain available.
notes: Every stroke creates a new centripetal spline, structural linework, translucent surfaces, and camera route. Nothing is prerecorded.
Draw one open, generous line. Crossings, closed loops, and bends tighter than the corridor width are rejected. Narrow the passage or increase smoothing to recover a tight drawing.
Select Edit points to reshape the spline. Enter drawing moves into the passage; scrolling or dragging vertically travels in either direction. Return to paper and Erase are always available.
The rising staircase gains height along the actual path. A spiral therefore becomes a helical stair passage. Structural surfaces are intentionally unfinished.

Drawing points rebuild the architecture on release. Setting changes are debounced; the renderer batches linework and rests between interactions. This study is intentionally excluded from simultaneous comparison.
reuse: Download the complete source with your current settings; it includes your drawn path and an offline copy of the Three.js runtime with its license.
Serve the extracted folder over HTTP and open example.html. No package installation or external CDN is needed for this example.
Import mount from index.js for the complete instrument, or generateEnvironment from geometry.js to use the procedural scene in your own Three.js application.
Pass normalized [x, y] coordinate pairs and settings. See the reuse guide for camera sampling, lifecycle cleanup, and the path JSON schema.
